title: Dhammas: the five heaps

cards: Point to yourself. Go ahead. Where did your finger land?
Maybe the middle of your chest. But is that you? Your chest is a body part.
Your feelings are somewhere else. Your thoughts seem to be up in your head. Your memories aren't anywhere you can point to at all.
People say I all day long, and it sounds like one solid thing. The Buddha suggested that if you look closely, what you call I comes apart into five heaps. Today's word: khandha.

teach.b: Khandha means a heap, a bundle, a mass, like a bundle of sticks.

teach.h: WHAT WE CALL A PERSON: FIVE OF THEM.
teach.b: The Buddha taught that what's called a person can be seen as five of them. Form, rupa: the body and the physical world. Feeling, vedana: pleasant, painful, neither, the second foundation.
Perception, sanna: recognizing, labeling, that's a cup, that's my friend. Formations, sankhara: intentions, habits, the urges and choices that shape what you do.
And consciousness, vinnana: the plain knowing of anything at all.
The sutta's instruction for each heap: such is form, such is its arising, such is its passing away. The same for feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Why sort yourself into heaps?

Because in the Buddha's teaching, each heap, looked at closely, is changing all the time, and none of them, on its own, is a solid owner in charge of the rest. That's what the Buddha pointed to with anatta, not-self.
As it's usually taught, it isn't a claim that nobody is here. It's that a self of one piece, fixed and in control, isn't found in any of the five. Elsewhere the Buddha gives a picture for each.
Form is like a lump of foam on a river. Feeling, a bubble on the water. Perception, a mirage.

teach.h: FOAM, BUBBLE, MIRAGE, BANANA TREE, TRICK.
teach.b: Formations, the trunk of a banana tree, layer after layer and no hard core.

how: The five aggregates are taught widely in Buddhist schools; practitioners contemplate them to see that each is changing and that no lasting, controlling self is found among them.

o: one of five heaps a person can be sorted into
a layer of the soul that lives on after death
a bad habit that piles up over many lives

games.q: match each heap to its picture.
p: a lump of foam on a river
a banana tree with no hard core

s: the teaching of not-self says you don't exist
it says a solid, controlling self isn't found in any of the five heaps.
khandha literally means a heap or bundle
the Buddha compares consciousness to a magician's trick
one of five pictures for the five heaps.

games.q: you hear a car pass. which heap is the label 'that's a car'?
games.why: perception, sanna, is recognizing and labeling. the sound is form, its tone is feeling.

practice: Take one moment, like a car passing, and sort it into five: form, the sound and your ear; feeling, pleasant, painful or neither; perception, the label, a car; formations, any urge, wishing it would stop, wondering where it's going; consciousness, the plain knowing of it all.
Five heaps, one moment. Then let it go, and wait for the next one.

wordCard.voice: Khandha. A heap: the Buddha's five, form, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness, each one arising and passing.

orig.note: Pali khandha (Sanskrit skandha): a heap, bundle or aggregate.

carryVoice: Your line: five heaps. Sorted into five, one moment can look a little less solid. Day two hundred sixty-one, done.

sources.ref: Majjhima Nikāya 10 (Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta), the five aggregates
